source: RULIP Project (Rural Livelihoods Improvement Project) / IFAD leaflet on the plastic-sheet Trap Barrier System for rice-field rat control
text:
Rice-field rats (កណ្ដុរស្រែ) are a significant yield-loss cause, especially cutting stems and gnawing developing panicles at field edges. A low-cost community-level control method is the plastic-sheet Trap Barrier System (TBS): erect a plastic-sheet fence enclosing a small plot planted with an attractant 'trap crop' rice sown a couple of weeks earlier than the surrounding main field, so it tillers and looks more attractive to rats first. Several multi-catch funnel traps are set into the fence at points along the barrier where rats naturally travel while trying to reach the attractant crop, rather than scattered randomly.

For the system to work, set it up before the main field reaches the growth stage rats target, keep the fence intact and free of gaps or holes rats can pass through, and check and clear traps regularly rather than leaving them unattended for days. TBS units are most effective when several are coordinated across a farming community at the same time rather than a single farmer installing one in isolation, since an untreated neighboring field simply pushes the rat population toward it instead of reducing the area-wide population.
